meta.title: The Hub
meta.description: The hub: the persistent meta-town you live in between runs. Its 11 buildable areas, all 48 workbench upgrades with costs and requirements, up to 10 wandering PC Pokémon, home styles and decor, and the hub's simulated clock, seasons and weather. The hub is functionally identical between Vanilla and EX, except three Market/Lab upgrades behave differently and one decor set is EX-only.

prose.heading: What the hub is
prose.text: The hub (named “Pokémon Hub” on your save) is the persistent town you live in between runs — it never resets. It is laid out as a grid of connected areas that you grow yourself: when you start, four areas are already built in a random chain (Labs, the Town Exit, the Safari Area and the Town Square), and everything else is constructed by the player. A run always starts at the Town Exit; when the run ends, your remaining party and Day Care Pokémon are added to the Safari Zone, and the run's rewards (money, Build Parts, items and decorations) come home with you to fund the next round of construction.

prose.heading: Building areas and upgrades
prose.text: Every area contains a workbench that opens the hub build shop — the Areas and Upgrades menus — both paid for with Build Parts, an item you earn from quest rewards. New areas must be built on a free connection of an area you already own, and the Challenge Area additionally requires you to have met Pokabbie. Upgrades live in one target area and can require that area plus up to two prerequisite upgrades — the cards list each requirement, and a few reserved placeholders require themselves, so they can never be built.

prose.heading: Wandering Pokémon
prose.text: Up to 10 Pokémon from your PC boxes appear as visible wandering Pokémon around your home — 5 in the Home Base exterior and 5 inside your house. They are picked starting from the highest-numbered PC box and working down to the first. The lineup refreshes every time you return from an adventure or make changes in your PC, so you can influence who shows up by which box a Pokémon is stored in.

prose.heading: Time, seasons and weather
prose.text: The hub runs on a simulated clock that only moves when you warp between maps — each warp during an active run adds 60 in-game minutes, and each warp while you're in the hub adds 15; there is no real-time clock. Whenever a new day or noon rolls over — and you are not in the middle of an adventure — the hub's weather re-rolls. The bed in your Home Base lets you sleep until a chosen wake time (Dawn, Day, Dusk or Night) and pick which season to wake up in, which is how you set the hub's clock.

prose.heading: The hub in the run loop
prose.text: Everything you earn in a run feeds back into the hub: Build Parts unlock the areas and upgrades above, berries keep growing in the Berry Fields while you are away, your leftover Pokémon keep the Safari Zone stocked for catch practice, and upgrades progressively open the meta-game's depth — Unique Lab tracking of your special catches, Day Care expansion, market blending, the Challenge Area's postgame quests, and the Legends Cave for re-battling your legendaries. The hub is where “one more run” gets funded and justified.

records.name: Labs
records.description: The hub's research district, present from the start: Professor Elm's Lab — the Config Lab where you adjust run settings — plus a dilapidated “Unique Lab” that tracks your special Unique Pokémon and the sets they can run. Its in-game sign text is still a development placeholder in both versions.

records.name: Town Exit (Adventure Entrance)
records.description: Present from the start — the gateway where every adventure begins. Its workbench hosts the entrance upgrades (randomised starter bag, and saving/replaying adventures), and it is the warp target when your run ends or is abandoned.
records.source: src/data/rogue_hub.h @vanilla L91-107 (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L381-389 / @origin/expansion L381-389 (run end → hub Town Exit)

records.name: Home Base
records.description: “Personal area to decorate & change outfits.” It has a bed for setting the time and season, interior and exterior decor, outfit selection, and hosts the wandering Pokémon visible from your PC.
records.source: src/data/rogue_hub.h @vanilla L108-126 (identical @origin/expansion); data/scripts/Rogue/Strings/Rogue_Strings_Items.pory @vanilla L391-395 (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_script.c @vanilla L1227-1276 (bed: time & season)

records.name: Berry Fields
records.description: “Grow berries and craft basic potions.” Berry plots keep growing while you are away on adventures; with the Potion Cauldron upgrade you can also brew basic potions from your harvest.

records.name: Safari Area
records.description: Present from the start — the home of the hub's Safari Zone, where Pokémon you release or lose in runs come back as catchable encounters. Contains the “View / Dismiss Pokémon” sign and, once unlocked by the “True Legend” quest, the Legends Cave entrance.

records.name: Park (Ride Training)
records.description: “Train Pokémon to help you in the Overworld.” The park is where ride-style Pokémon that assist you around the overworld are trained.

records.name: Poké Marts
records.description: “Shops for TMs, Poké Balls, held items etc.” The hub's shopping district: a general mart plus upgradeable Poké Ball, TM, battle-enhancer and held-item shops.

records.name: Town Square
records.description: Present from the start — the hub's central plaza. It hosts the Trainer School building (tips and tricks for adventures), the Move Tutor, and a workbench. Its in-game sign text is still a development placeholder in both versions.

records.name: Challenge Area
records.description: “Access various new quests and items…” A free-to-build postgame area that only becomes available after meeting Pokabbie; it is the hub's home for Challenge-based quests (such as the region-style battles and, in EX, the Z-A Royale).
records.source: src/data/rogue_hub.h @vanilla L223-241 (identical @origin/expansion); data/scripts/Rogue/Strings/Rogue_Strings_Items.pory @vanilla L381-385 (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_hub.c @vanilla L1002-1013 / @origin/expansion L1002-1013 (Pokabbie requirement)

records.name: Day Care
records.description: “Bring extra Pokémon into adventures and hatch eggs.” Day Care Pokémon join your run alongside your party, and upgrades add capacity, breeders, remote Pokégear access, a tea room and experience share for your Day Care Pokémon.

records.name: Market
records.description: “Blend Pokéblocks and improve Pokémon IVs.” The market's blender, bakery and bank upgrades support the IV-improvement pipeline; the Treat Shop sells Mints in EX but Pokéblocks in Vanilla.

records.name: Interior Base
records.description: An interior space to decorate in the Home Base.

records.name: Upper Floor
records.description: Reserved — not yet functional in either version (it requires itself, so it can never be built). Planned: “a 2nd floor with a bed allowing you to rest until a specific time.”

records.name: Town Style
records.description: “Change styles from Home Base e.g. Path” — unlocks the area style (Overgrown, Flowers or Plain), building style and path restyling for your home.

records.name: Unique Lab
records.description: Hidden upgrade — it cannot be bought and is only granted as a quest reward (the regional-style quest chain). It is the foundation of the Unique Lab: the dilapidated lab that tracks the special “Unique” Pokémon you catch.
records.source: src/data/rogue_hub.h @vanilla L316-322 (isHidden, identical @origin/expansion); src/data/rogue/quests/region_style.json @vanilla L78 (identical @origin/expansion, quest reward)

records.name: Unique Pokémon Types
records.description: “Unique Pokémon can have alternative typing.” How you obtain it differs by version: Vanilla sells it; EX hides it and grants it as a quest reward from the Z-A Royale challenge instead.

differences.vanilla: Purchasable for 9 Build Parts in the Labs, requiring “Exotic Unique Pokémon”.
differences.ex: Hidden (not purchasable); granted as a quest reward by the “Z-A Royale” challenge (2.1.0_region_style.json).

records.name: Legend Cave
records.description: Hidden upgrade — it cannot be bought and is only granted as a quest reward: complete “True Legend” (catch a legendary during an adventure). It opens the Legends Cave entrance on the Safari Area, where you can re-battle legendaries you have caught by offering them Pokéblocks they like.

records.name: Bank
records.description: “Increase starting money for adventures.”

records.name: Home styles and decor
records.description: After the “Town Style” upgrade you can restyle your Home Base: 3 area styles (Overgrown, Flowers, Plain), 5 building styles (Cave, Trees, Red Brick, Wooden, Gym) applied to the house exterior, interior and the surrounding path. Decor — 160 exterior and 32 interior slots — is unlocked as quest rewards (the decor quest reward) and placed from the decor menu. The “Appliances” decor set (Rotom) is the only version split: its source block is compiled into EX builds only.

differences.vanilla: The decor menu excludes the “Appliances” set (the code skips it in non-Expansion builds).
differences.ex: The “Appliances” decor set is available, unlocked through the Rotom mastery quest (EX-only quest data).
